Water molecules sticking to each other, producing surface tension
Water molecules sticking to other surfaces, enabling capillary action

Breaking a polymer by adding a water molecule

A fatty acid with one or more double bonds, liquid at room temperature
The linear sequence of amino acids
The overall three-dimensional folded shape of a polypeptide
DNA and RNA strands run 5 prime to 3 prime
Cell Structure and Function: Surface area to volume ratio
The constraint limiting how large a cell can grow
Endosymbiotic theory
Mitochondria and chloroplasts arose from engulfed prokaryotes
Rough endoplasmic reticulum
ER studded with ribosomes that processes proteins
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
ER that synthesises lipids and detoxifies compounds
Selective permeability
A membrane letting some substances cross but not others
Fluid mosaic model
The membrane as a flexible lipid bilayer with embedded proteins
Aquaporin
A channel protein allowing rapid water movement
Facilitated diffusion
Passive transport through a protein, requiring no energy
Sodium-potassium pump
An active transporter moving three sodium out for every two potassium in
Water potential
The measure predicting the direction of water movement
Plasmolysis
A plant cell shrinking away from its wall in a hypertonic solution
Turgor pressure
Internal water pressure keeping a plant cell firm

The active site changing shape slightly to grip its substrate
A molecule blocking the active site directly
A molecule binding elsewhere and changing the enzyme's shape
Control of enzyme activity by binding at a site other than the active site
The energy barrier a reaction must overcome
A reaction requiring an input of free energy
ATP production driven by a proton gradient across a membrane
A membrane series of carriers building the proton gradient
Thylakoid reactions producing ATP and NADPH from light
Stroma reactions fixing carbon dioxide into sugar

Cell Communication and Cell Cycle: Signal transduction pathway
The relay converting an external signal into a cellular response
Ligand
A signalling molecule that binds a receptor
Receptor protein
A protein that detects a specific signal molecule
Second messenger
A small molecule relaying a signal inside the cell, such as cyclic AMP
Amplification in signalling
One signal molecule triggering a large cascading response
Negative feedback
A response reversing the original change, maintaining stability
Positive feedback
A response amplifying the original change, driving it to completion
Checkpoint
A control point verifying the cell is ready to proceed in the cycle
Cyclin
A regulatory protein whose level rises and falls to drive the cell cycle
Apoptosis
Programmed cell death that removes damaged or unneeded cells
Cancer
Uncontrolled cell division resulting from failed cycle regulation
G1, S, and G2 phases
The growth, DNA synthesis, and preparation stages of interphase
Heredity: Law of segregation
Allele pairs separate during gamete formation
Law of independent assortment
Genes on different chromosomes are inherited independently
Test cross
Crossing with a homozygous recessive to reveal an unknown genotype
Dihybrid cross
A cross tracking two traits at once, giving a 9:3:3:1 ratio
Linked genes
Genes close together on a chromosome that tend to be inherited together
Recombination frequency
How often linked genes separate, used to map chromosomes
Sex-linked trait
A trait carried on a sex chromosome, usually the X
Nondisjunction
Chromosomes failing to separate properly during meiosis
Pedigree
A family diagram used to trace inheritance patterns
Epistasis
One gene masking or modifying the expression of another
Polygenic trait
A trait controlled by many genes, producing continuous variation
Chi-square test
A statistical test comparing observed results to expected ratios
Gene Expression and Regulation: Transcription
Synthesising an RNA copy of a DNA template
Translation
Assembling a polypeptide from an mRNA sequence at the ribosome
Promoter
The DNA region where RNA polymerase binds to begin transcription
Operon
A cluster of genes in prokaryotes transcribed together under one promoter
lac operon
An inducible bacterial operon switched on in the presence of lactose
trp operon
A repressible bacterial operon switched off when tryptophan is abundant
RNA splicing
Removing introns and joining exons in eukaryotic mRNA
Intron
A non-coding stretch removed from pre-mRNA
Exon
A coding stretch retained in mature mRNA
Epigenetics
Heritable changes in gene expression without altering the DNA sequence
Transcription factor
A protein controlling whether a gene is transcribed
Point mutation
A change to a single nucleotide
Frameshift mutation
An insertion or deletion shifting the entire reading frame
Gel electrophoresis
Separating DNA fragments by size in an electric field
Natural Selection: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
The state where allele frequencies stay constant across generations
Hardy-Weinberg conditions
No mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating, and large population
Genetic drift
Random change in allele frequency, strongest in small populations
Bottleneck effect
Loss of genetic variation after a sharp population crash
Founder effect
Reduced variation when a few individuals start a new population
Directional selection
Selection favouring one extreme of a trait
Stabilizing selection
Selection favouring the intermediate and reducing variation
Disruptive selection
Selection favouring both extremes over the middle
Sexual selection
Selection driven by success in obtaining mates
Allopatric speciation
New species forming after geographic separation
Sympatric speciation
New species forming without geographic separation
Convergent evolution
Unrelated lineages evolving similar traits under similar pressures
Phylogenetic tree
A branching diagram of evolutionary relationships
Common ancestry evidence
Shared DNA, homologous structures, and the universal genetic code
Ecology: Population density
The number of individuals per unit area
Exponential growth
Unlimited growth producing a J-shaped curve
Logistic growth
Growth slowing near carrying capacity, producing an S-shaped curve
Carrying capacity
The maximum population an environment can sustain
Density-dependent factor
A limiting factor whose effect grows with crowding, such as disease
Density-independent factor
A limiting factor unaffected by population size, such as a storm
Trophic level
A feeding position within an energy pyramid
Ten percent rule
Roughly a tenth of energy transfers to the next trophic level
Primary productivity
The rate at which producers convert energy into biomass
Keystone species
A species whose removal dramatically restructures its community
Ecological succession
Predictable change in community composition over time
Biogeochemical cycle
The movement of an element such as carbon or nitrogen through an ecosystem
Nitrogen fixation
Bacteria converting atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form
Simpson's diversity index
A calculated measure of species diversity in a community
